root_causes: The critical evidence (spirit identity) is encoded only as a small, unlabeled icon shape in the HUD, not as on-screen text, making this a hard icon-recognition task rather than an OCR task for the visual sub-agent.

clip_qa crop choice was highly inconsistent across rollouts (crop sizes ranging from a full 1000x1000 frame down to a ~140x220px sliver); overly tight crops (rollout 0, 3) removed contextual cues and led to misidentification, while a crop that preserved the icon in its ring/gem context (rollout 2) led to a correct read.
One rollout (1) picked the wrong time window entirely despite having already found the correct one via semantic_search, confusing a different unrelated boss encounter for the Red Boy fight.

Two rollouts (3, 4) show clip_qa producing confident but unsupported readings (a ginseng-shape guess, and a fabricated ability-HUD text label) when the actual icon has no visible name text -- consistent with vision-model hallucination under ambiguous/illegible input rather than faithful 'not visible' reporting.
what_worked: Rollout 2's clip_qa used a crop wide enough to keep the spirit icon's full circular border and adjacent gem markers visible, which preserved enough shape detail for a wolf silhouette to be correctly recognized as 地狼.
Text retrieval (semantic_search + run_sql over episodes/topic_facts/entities) reliably located the correct 75390-75480s Red Boy time window in 4 of 5 rollouts.
transferable_lessons: When the visible evidence is an icon/silhouette rather than legible text, instruct clip_qa to use a crop that preserves surrounding context (the icon's frame/border/other HUD elements) rather than zooming in tightly on just the icon -- over-zooming lost the shape cues needed for correct icon recognition.

If clip_qa returns a confident answer without evidence of a legible name/text, treat it with more skepticism and consider a second confirming call with a different crop/frame before submitting, since vision sub-agents can guess plausible-sounding names from ambiguous icons instead of reporting 'not legible'.

When a strong textual match is already found for a claimed event's time window (e.g. explicit '红孩儿' entity tag), don't let a later, weaker semantic-search hit for a superficially similar scene override the earlier stronger match -- verify against the original candidate first.

For HUD-icon identification questions, prefer game-domain knowledge of icon conventions (e.g. known spirit icon set) as a secondary check alongside the visual read, since icon shapes alone can be genuinely ambiguous at low resolution.
